hero.title: Egypt, through the eyes of a local
hero.sub: Family-run tours and a guest house 800 metres from the Sphinx, since 2014.

home.introTitle: Come as friends, leave as family
home.intro1: I am Rami. I grew up in the shadow of the pyramids in a Bedouin family, and in 2014 a friend asked me to show her the real Egypt. I have been doing it ever since, with my sister Rania and a small team, from our family home in Giza.
home.intro2: We do history properly, we eat with you, and we go to the places the buses do not. Every tip at every site is already paid, so you will not be hassled. And every trip can be changed to fit you.

history.title: Local expert history
history.text: Inside the third pyramid, the tomb of Irukaptah, the Osireion at Abydos: guides who grew up here and read the walls.

culture.title: Culture and traditions
culture.text: Sufi night in Islamic Cairo, bread baked in the sand with our Bedouin hosts, breakfast cooked by my mother.

hidden.title: Hidden gems
hidden.text: Fayoum's whale fossils, Abusir at dusk, Amarna, the White Desert. Places you will have almost to yourself.

home.mapTitle: From the delta to Abu Simbel
home.mapText: Every destination below has a page, and most appear in several itineraries. Tap a pin.
home.toursText: From four days around Cairo to three weeks that end in the White Desert. All prices include tickets, breakfast, lunch, tips at the sites and private transport.
home.stayText: Seven rooms in our family home, a rooftop facing the pyramids, and the sound-and-light show from your chair. Every tour starts here.
home.teamText: Rami grew up on the plateau and started hosting travellers in 2014. Rania, his sister, guides too, and many of our solo women guests ask for her. Between them, Kelly and Ehab, there is always someone at the house.
home.ctaText: Send a WhatsApp or the form and you will have a plan and a price within a day.

tours.title: Nine itineraries, all of them yours to change
tours.lead: Prices are per person in US dollars and include the room, every ticket, breakfast and lunch, tips at the sites and private transport. Students pay less; children under five pay half.

tour.itineraryText: Every day below can be moved or swapped. Tell us what matters to you.
tour.staysText: In Cairo you stay at Pyramids Temple Guest House unless you prefer a hotel. Elsewhere, 3-star hotels we have used for years, or as listed.
customSteps: Tell us your dates, who is coming, and what you want to see. Not sure? Say what you like.

stay.roomsText: Simple, clean and quiet, each named after a pyramid on its door. Air conditioning, a kitchenette, blackout curtains, towels with the house name on them. Swipe a card for more photos; prices are confirmed when you ask.

about.title: A message during Ramadan, 2014
about.p1: During Ramadan in 2014 I got a message on Couchsurfing from Nicki, an American who was coming to Egypt and wanted to see the real one. I showed her Giza the way I knew it, from the dunes, with tea at my mother's table. Two weeks later she asked if her family friend Jeremy could come too. I invited him to stay at our house.
about.p2: Five months later my inbox was full of people asking for the same thing. I needed a name. My grandfather had been a government tour guide in 1964, and after he died I wanted to carry that on. Rami's Insight Tours was born on the rooftop.
about.p3: We are a Bedouin family from the desert, and hospitality is not a business model for us, it is how we were raised. You eat with us. You meet my mother. My sister Rania guides too, and many of our women guests ask for her. The house you sleep in is ours.
about.p4: We work with a small team: Rania, Kelly, Ehab, drivers we have known for years, and Bedouin hosts at Abusir and in the White Desert. We know the guards and the camel owners by name, which is why nothing at the pyramids costs you extra.
about.t1964: Rami's grandfather guides for the government
about.t2014: Nicki's message; the first guests stay at the house
about.tNow: Nine itineraries, two guest houses, guests from forty countries
about.raniaText: Rania grew up here too. She guides Cairo and the Nile, talks openly about life and society in Egypt, and is the reason so many solo women write to us afterwards. Ask for her when you book.

how.title: Tips are on us
how.text: Every guard, every camel, every tomb door at the sites is paid in advance.

how.title: You eat with the family
how.text: Breakfast on the rooftop, lunch wherever we are, dinners you will not forget.

how.title: We pick you up
how.text: At the airport, with your name on a sign, at any hour.

how.title: Everything can change
how.text: Nothing on this site is fixed. Tell us what matters and we rebuild the days.
